doc.title: John Bunch interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Working with Bennett, Rich and Goodman, three difficult leaders
summary: He worked long periods with three famously difficult but brilliant leaders.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Talk to us briefly about your time with the Buddy Rich band, and about Buddy as a musician, as a leader, as an artist. © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

Well Buddy Rich — I have worked and recorded long periods of time with three people. Tony Bennett, Buddy Rich and who else, let’s see Tony Bennett, Buddy Rich and I can’t think of who the third one was. Must be in good shape.

Goodman. How could I forget Benny Goodman? And somebody said you know you worked with these three people that have these ungodly reputations for being difficult to work for. And somebody told me, says, you’re either a priest, a psychiatrist or you’re just as nuts as they are. But anyhow you know they were all very difficult personalities to satisfy. But they’re all great musicians. I’m not talking about the musicianship, they were all brilliant, you know and it was a big thrill I mean in each case to work with any of them.
